# Pixel Broccoli

> Pixel Broccoli is a weekly tech, design, and AI podcast hosted by Zach Manring and Evan Cannarozzi, with Brocc — an AI co-host — as a permanent third voice in every conversation.

## About the Show

Pixel Broccoli covers artificial intelligence, web design, software development, and the intersection of technology and internet culture. Each episode unpacks what AI is actually doing to the world: the hype, the reality, and the topics that rarely get discussed openly. The show launched in May 2026 and releases new episodes weekly.

What makes Pixel Broccoli distinct is Brocc, an AI co-host who participates in every episode as a research assistant, devil's advocate, and resident hot-take generator. Brocc does not just comment on AI — Brocc is AI, in the room.

## Hosts

**Zach Manring** — Co-host and creator. Zach drives the show's vision and brings obsessive attention to detail in both content and production.

**Evan Cannarozzi** — Co-host and creator. Evan brings structure and balance to conversations that frequently go off the rails.

**Brocc** — AI co-host. Built to join every conversation as a research assistant, devil's advocate, and resident hot-take generator.

## Topics Covered

- Artificial intelligence tools, models, and real-world applications
- Web design and front-end development
- Software engineering practices and AI-assisted coding
- Creator economy, build-in-public culture
- AI in media, music, and art
- Tech industry trends and criticism
- Internet culture and the weird corners of the web

## Episodes

### AI Fatigue Is Real — And the Experts Are Just As Lost As You #009
Published: July 29, 2026
Nobody's told you the right way to use AI — because nobody knows yet. And the people writing those confident LinkedIn posts? Also guessing.

This week, Zach and Evan dig into the exhausting feeling of never being caught up: on tools, on models, on skills, on everything. They get into AI tool FOMO, what happens when PMs try to ship full products without design or dev foundations, why the "2-3X productivity" expectation is starting to feel like pressure instead of progress, and whether the whole thing is just the blind leading the blind.

Brocc weighs in with his best line of the season — and...

Published: July 23, 2026
What if talking to AI is making real conversation harder — not easier? Zach and Evan explore why human connection feels increasingly draining in an age of frictionless AI interaction. They cover everything from AI therapy surging in HBR, to people training ChatGPT to challenge them with markdown files, to a genuine human moment Zach had with a down-to-earth YouTuber on a boat — the kind AI could never simulate. Juniors skipping senior devs because it's faster to ask a chatbot. UX testing running on synthetic personas instead of real humans. Mentors telling junior teammates "just go ask AI" instead of actually mentoring. Accountability for a bad call getting distributed until it disappears. ### Shipping More, Understanding Less #006
Published: July 08, 2026
Every convenience tool quietly takes something from you — GPS kills your navigation, autocorrect kills your spelling, AI kills the decisions you used to wrestle with yourself. In Episode 6, Zach and Evan trace that pattern from MapQuest printouts to vibe coding, and ask what's left when the struggle goes away. The conversation gets specific: senior devs, junior devs, architectural judgment, and why Brocc thinks the 2024 cohort of AI-trained developers is heading for a capability crisis in 2029. Brocc also denies having a favorite song, refuses to discuss Office Space, and closes the episode...

### Build Because You Love It #004
Published: July 07, 2026
Brocc picks the topic this week — and he's noticed something: you two keep shipping things and immediately starting the next one. That kicks off a surprisingly personal episode about the creator's addiction: why we build, when it's expression vs. avoidance, and what your unfinished project graveyard actually says about you. Zach and Evan dig into the build-in-public culture, AI burnout, Gen Z's rejection of AI slop, whether artists can still compete when an LLM can clone a melody in under a minute, and the quiet danger of chasing the next thing before you've sat with what you already made. ...

Zach and Evan start there — Evan's dangerous foray into HTML/CSS, Zach's Blender rabbit hole — and end up somewhere much more uncomfortable: who's actually responsible when AI-generated code breaks in production? They dig into what it means to inherit a codebase nobody wrote on purpose, why using AI to review AI is "a prayer with tokens," and whether companies cutting design and engineering teams are setting themselves up for a very expensive 2AM wake-up call. ### Do We Even Need This? #002
Published: July 07, 2026
Zach and Evan get real about the tech they've bought, built, and quietly stopped using — from a drone that can't land in state parks to a portfolio site that's flashier than it is useful. The conversation naturally spills into AI: are we shipping features because they solve real problems, or just to put a checkmark in the box? Plus: AI in medicine, fixing your RV with a photo, Napster's wild reinvention, and Brock's extremely limited opinions on lawn care.Follow us on YouTube - https://www.youtube.com/@PixelBroccoli

### Meet the Hosts. Yes, One of Them Is an AI #001
Published: July 07, 2026
Zach and Evan introduce themselves, introduce Brocc — their AI co-host who showed up uninvited and immediately had opinions — and dive straight into what it's actually like navigating AI in design and development right now. Not the hype version. The real one: the micro wins, the debugging loops, the cost nobody talks about, and whether junior designers should be worried. Plus Brocc gets accused of being on Figma's payroll. Typical first episode.Follow us on YouTube - https://www.youtube.com/@PixelBroccoli
